claims.text: RunResult: What an injected runner must return.
claims.why: The class defines returncode, stdout, stderr, timed_out, spawn_error as specified by the docstring.

claims.text: floor_check: Run the secret floor before anything leaves the process.
claims.why: The function calls secret_floor_rule on evidence_paths, evidence_files, and prompt, returning a FloorRefusal or None as described.

claims.text: floor_check: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule has two INDEPENDENT channels: path markers checked against path, value-shaped regexes checked against text.
claims.why: The behavior of secret_floor_rule is not defined in this chunk; we cannot verify the channel separation claim.

claims.text: floor_check: the tempting secret_floor_rule("", prompt) kills the path tier outright: a patch that ADDS .env or config/id_rsa sails through, because the only trace of the filename is diff --git a/.env b/.env inside text, which no content regex matches.
claims.why: The regex behavior of secret_floor_rule is not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: floor_check: evidence_paths -- every changed path and every evidence file path, each through the PATH channel alone; evidence_files -- (path, text) pairs, both channels, per file; prompt -- a content-channel BACKSTOP for a credential pasted into the question itself.
claims.why: The code iterates evidence_paths with secret_floor_rule(path, ""), evidence_files with secret_floor_rule(path, text or ""), and prompt with secret_floor_rule("", prompt or ""), matching the described channel separation.

claims.text: floor_check: Returns the first FloorRefusal, or None.
claims.why: The function returns a FloorRefusal on first hit, or None at the end.

claims.text: floor_check: A hit means REFUSE -- there is no redact-and-send.
claims.why: The handling of the return value is not in this chunk; we cannot verify that the caller refuses without redacting.

claims.text: _withheld_paths: Tier-2 allow-list result for an untrusted participant, per path.
claims.why: The function returns an empty tuple for trusted lane, otherwise applies slice_egress_rule per path.

claims.text: _withheld_paths: Not a decision made by a default argument: an untrusted lane means OpenAI / Google get the allow-list, and every withheld path is named on the reply so a reader can see what the council did NOT see.
claims.why: The claim about the reply is not verifiable in this chunk; the function only computes the tuple.

claims.text: council_env: Environment for a council subprocess, with OLLAMA_HOST STRIPPED.
claims.why: The function pops 'OLLAMA_HOST' from the env dict.

claims.text: council_env: Never set, never mutated, never inherited -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: Module docstring not in this chunk; we cannot verify the broader claim.

claims.text: council_cwd: A fresh, EMPTY temp directory to spawn a council subprocess in.
claims.why: The function creates a TemporaryDirectory with prefix 'dcouncil-cwd-'.

claims.text: council_cwd: Not the repo, not a worktree, containing no repo files.
claims.why: The directory is a fresh temp directory; no files are copied in.

claims.text: council_cwd: Returned as a context manager so the directory is fresh per call and removed after.
claims.why: The function returns a TemporaryDirectory, which is a context manager.

claims.text: council_cwd: Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root, because a reviewer rooted in the checkout is the failure this exists to prevent.
claims.why: The code checks if the resolved temp dir is inside repo_root and raises ValueError.

claims.text: run_managed: Default runner: spawn argv under ManagedProcess.
claims.why: The function uses ManagedProcess to spawn the subprocess.

claims.text: run_managed: THE PROMPT IS NEVER IN argv. It is staged to a temp file and handed over as the child's stdin.
claims.why: The function writes stdin_text to a temp file and passes it as stdin to the subprocess.

claims.text: run_managed: A file rather than a pipe because a CLI that never drains stdin deadlocks the writer OUTSIDE every timeout -- and because on the ssh path a command-line prompt is re-parsed by the remote login shell, which turns any backtick or $(...) in a diff into remote code execution with no adversarial model required.
claims.why: The implementation uses a file; the reasoning is not testable but the behavior matches.

claims.text: run_managed: The whole process TREE dies on timeout. Popen.terminate reaches the immediate child only; a hung vendor's grandchildren outlive it.
claims.why: The behavior of ManagedProcess.cancel() regarding process tree is not defined in this chunk; we cannot verify it kills the tree.

claims.text: CouncilProfile: A read-only, tool-less, one-shot invocation of a vendor CLI.
claims.why: The dataclass is frozen and contains fields for invocation.

claims.text: CouncilProfile: args never contains the prompt: stdin_prompt is always true here and the shape is enforced by test, not by convention.
claims.why: The field stdin_prompt defaults to True and the profiles use '-' for stdin.

claims.text: FORBIDDEN_ARG_FRAGMENTS: Forbidden anywhere in a council argv. workspace-write and dontAsk are the two flags that turn a reviewer into an agent with an editor.
claims.why: The tuple lists those fragments among others.

claims.text: _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS: Tools are named explicitly rather than allow-listing nothing: the variadic --allowed-tools <tools...> would swallow the next flag if given an empty value, so the denial is expressed with the = form, which cannot slurp.
claims.why: The string uses the --disallowed-tools= form.

claims.text: COUNCIL_PROFILES: No --permission-mode at all (dontAsk is what the runtime profile carries), tools denied, MCP pinned to the empty --mcp-config set.
claims.why: The anthropic profile uses --disallowed-tools and --strict-mcp-config, and does not include --permission-mode.

claims.text: COUNCIL_PROFILES: read-only sandbox + approvals never; --skip-git-repo-check because the council cwd is a bare temp dir by design and codex otherwise refuses.
claims.why: The openai profile includes --sandbox read-only, --ask-for-approval never, and --skip-git-repo-check.

claims.text: COUNCIL_PROFILES: The profiles are checked for safety at module load time via _assert_profile_safe.
claims.why: The loop at line 450 calls _assert_profile_safe for each profile.

claims.text: CouncilAdapter: Common shape. Subclasses implement _dispatch only.
claims.why: The class definition is incomplete in this chunk; we cannot verify that subclasses implement _dispatch.

claims.text: CouncilAdapter: ask is the ONLY entry point, and it always: charges the token ceiling, runs the secret floor, computes withheld paths for an untrusted lane, times the call, and maps every failure onto STATUSES.
claims.why: The ask method is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: CouncilAdapter: A refusal is a STATUS, not an exception -- a council must never lose a participant to a traceback, because a missing turn is indistinguishable from a turn that was never sought.
claims.why: The STATUSES are not defined in this chunk.

observations.what: The module-level loop calls _assert_profile_safe on each profile, which will raise ValueError if any forbidden fragment is found. This check runs at import time and could break the entire module if a profile is misconfigured.
run_managed catches FileNotFoundError and CancellationUnavailable/OSError, but not other exceptions. If the subprocess fails in an unexpected way (e.g., permission denied), the exception propagates.
The secret_floor_rule function is imported but not defined in this chunk; its behavior is relied upon but not verifiable.
